exposure: genera (e.g., Erysipelatoclostridium, Mucispirillum, Finegoldia, Erysipelotrichaceae UCG-003, Sporolactobacillus)
cohort: The study included 29 women with uterine fibroids and 38 healthy women.
finding: The study revealed perturbations and distinct patterns in the vaginal and cervical microbiome, including increased Firmicutes and altered genera, in women with uterine fibroids compared to healthy women, suggesting reduced stability of their microbiota.
cross-section timing: Data was collected at a single point in time for each participant to profile the microbiome in women with and without uterine fibroids.
